safety.config.fix: How to fix: change the value in that file to meet the condition above, then run `lanekeeper-config validate` again.
explain.rule.override: higher layer wins (personal > plugin option > machine > project > default)
explain.rule.union: union of every layer (cannot be removed)
init.q.gate: Full verification command (leave empty if none)
init.gitignore: Note: `{pattern}` in .gitignore blocks `{path}`. Add the exception line `!{path}`.
init.notGit: Not a git repository. Skipping the state folder and exclude entry.
init.done: Initialization finished. Run `/lanekeeper:doctor` to review the result.
doctor.title: Lanekeeper check
doctor.codegraph.missing: not installed. `/lanekeeper:init` installs it only after you agree
safety.where: Run `/lanekeeper:doctor` or read the "Safety hooks" section of the README. Only the repository owner can change these rules.
safety.git.unresolved.why: The target folder or command of `{cmd}` cannot be known before it runs (variable or command substitution).
safety.git.unresolved.fix: Write the path and the git subcommand literally and run it again, e.g. `git -C /absolute/path commit -m "..."`.
safety.git.lane_commit.why: A lane may only commit on its own lane branch ({own}). The current branch is `{branch}`.
safety.git.lane_commit.fix: Commit from your own lane worktree. The main checkout, the integration branch and other lanes' branches belong to the main session.
safety.git.lane_commit_instruction.why: This repository allows lane commits only on instruction (project.lanes.commit = on-instruction). The brief of lane {lane} does not allow commits.
safety.git.lane_commit_instruction.fix: Do not commit; leave the changes in the working tree and report. When a commit is needed, the main session adds `commit=allowed` to the brief marker or a line "commit allowed" and dispatches again.
safety.git.lane_merge.why: A lane may only merge or rebase the latest integration branch into its own branch ({own}); current branch `{branch}`.
safety.git.lane_merge.fix: Name the integration branch explicitly, e.g. `git rebase <integration branch>`. Leave other merges to the main session.
safety.git.lane_push.fix: Commit on your own branch and report. The main session integrates and pushes.
safety.git.lane_switch.why: A lane may not switch to another branch (current `{branch}`).
safety.git.lane_switch.fix: Stay on your lane branch. To restore files only, use `git checkout -- <file>` or `git restore <file>`.
safety.git.stash.why: The stash list is shared with other sessions and worktrees; an unnamed stash or pop can take or drop someone else's changes.
safety.git.stash.fix: Use a temporary WIP commit, or `git stash push -u -m "<unique name>"` and restore with `git stash apply <sha>`.
safety.git.reset_hard.why: `git reset --hard` discards uncommitted changes for good (current `{branch}`).
safety.git.reset_hard.fix: Check what would be lost with `git status` first and leave a WIP commit if needed.
safety.git.clean.why: `git clean -f` deletes untracked files for good.
safety.git.branch_protected.why: The protected branch `{target}` cannot be deleted, moved or force-recreated.
safety.git.branch_protected.fix: Leave protected branches alone. If it must change, the repository owner runs it directly.
safety.git.branch_delete.why: This deletes or overwrites branch `{target}`. Unmerged commits can be lost.
safety.git.branch_delete.fix: Check for unmerged commits with `git log {target} --not --remotes`.
safety.git.ref.why: Editing branch refs directly bypasses the merge rules.
safety.git.ref.fix: Use the regular commands such as `git merge` or `git branch`.
safety.git.gate_locked.why: A verification gate is running (gate lock present). Merges wait until it finishes.
safety.git.gate_locked.fix: Run it again after the gate finishes. If the gate crashed, check the lock with `/lanekeeper:doctor`.
safety.git.main_merge.why: The protected branch `{branch}` takes a single source, and only with an owner grant.
safety.git.main_merge.fix: Name one branch to merge, have the repository owner type `/lanekeeper:approve merge-main <branch>`, then run it again.
safety.git.force_push.why: Force pushes (--force, --force-with-lease, +refspec) are not allowed for anyone.
safety.git.force_push.fix: Integrate the remote first (e.g. `git pull --rebase`) and push normally.
safety.git.push_all.fix: Name each branch to push, e.g. `git push origin <branch>`.
safety.git.push_feature.why: Feature branch pushes need confirmation (setting `project.git.feature_push: ask`).
safety.git.push_feature.fix: Confirm the push. To always allow it, set `git.feature_push` to `allow` in `.lanekeeper/config.json`.
safety.git.push_feature_denied.why: This project blocks pushes from agents (`project.git.feature_push: deny`).
safety.grant.missing.why: This action ({action}) on the protected branch `{branch}` needs an owner grant, and there is none.
safety.grant.missing.fix: The repository owner must type `/lanekeeper:approve {action}` in the prompt (15 minutes, one use, one commit). Agents cannot create grants.
safety.grant.action.why: The current grant is for a different action (needed: {action}).
safety.grant.used.why: The grant has already been used. Grants are single-use.
safety.grant.used.fix: If it is needed again, the repository owner types `/lanekeeper:approve {action}` again.
safety.grant.expired.fix: The repository owner must type `/lanekeeper:approve {action}` again.
safety.grant.head.why: The granted commit ({granted}) differs from the commit being applied ({head}).
safety.grant.head.fix: The branch moved after the grant. Review it again; the repository owner types `/lanekeeper:approve {action}` again.
safety.stamp.missing.why: There is no gate pass stamp for commit {head}.
safety.stamp.missing.fix: In the worktree that has the commit to merge checked out, pass `lanekeeper-test-report gate-pass` (runs project.gate.command) or `lanekeeper-test-report run` (full verification) to the end; that writes the stamp. Then run this again.
safety.stamp.head.why: The gate pass stamp belongs to another commit ({stamped}; needed: {head}).
safety.stamp.head.fix: Changes other than result files came in after the stamp. Run `lanekeeper-test-report gate-pass` or `lanekeeper-test-report run` again on this commit.
safety.gh.lane_merge.why: Lanes may not merge pull requests.
safety.gh.lane_merge.fix: Put the PR number in your report and leave the merge to the main session.
safety.gh.unresolved.why: The PR's base branch could not be determined, so the merge is blocked.
safety.gh.unresolved.fix: Check that `gh pr view <number>` works. A PR into a protected branch also needs `/lanekeeper:approve merge-main` first.
safety.kill.pattern.why: Killing by name or pattern (`{cmd}`) can take down other sessions' or the owner's servers.
safety.kill.pattern.fix: Find the PID of the process you started and use `kill <PID>`.
safety.kill.protected_port.fix: Protected-port servers belong to the owner. Use your lane ports (`lanekeeper-port get`).
safety.kill.unresolved.why: The target PID of `{cmd}` cannot be checked in advance, so protected ports cannot be ruled out.
safety.kill.unresolved.fix: Write the PID as a number and run it again.
safety.rm.dynamic.why: The `rm -r` target `{target}` depends on a variable or an unknown folder, so what it deletes is unknown.
safety.rm.dynamic.fix: Write the path to delete as an absolute path.
safety.rm.broad.why: Removing `{target}` wipes the home folder, a system folder or the whole project.
safety.rm.broad.fix: Name the exact subfolder to remove.
safety.rm.git.why: `{target}` is inside a git repository's internal folder.
safety.rm.git.fix: Clean up with git commands such as `git worktree remove` or `git gc`.
safety.rm.outside.fix: Make sure the path is safe to remove. Keep temporary files in a temp folder or inside the project.
safety.browser.headed.why: A browser that opens a window (`{cmd}`) steals focus from the person using the machine.
safety.browser.headed.fix: Add `--headless=new`, or run Playwright in its default headless mode. If a window is really needed, the owner runs it directly.
safety.browser.open.fix: Capture with a headless browser and share the result file.
safety.browser.playwright_window.fix: Use a headless run (`pnpm exec playwright test`) and the result files (trace, report).
safety.paths.state.why: `{path}` is a Lanekeeper state file (owner grant, gate stamp, lane ledger). Only hooks and Lanekeeper tools write it.
safety.paths.state.fix: Grants come from `/lanekeeper:approve` and stamps from a gate run. Do not edit them by hand.
safety.paths.accepted.why: `{path}` records which weakened test results the owner accepted. Only `/lanekeeper:approve accept-quality` writes it.
safety.paths.accepted.fix: Ask the repository owner to type `/lanekeeper:approve accept-quality <kind> --reason why` in the prompt, or revert the weakening.
safety.paths.ack.why: `{path}` holds the `bypassPermissions` acknowledgement of the automatic resume. Only a person can give it.
safety.paths.ack.fix: Ask the owner to type `/lanekeeper:approve retry-bypass` in the prompt. Other personal settings can be changed with the Write or Edit tool, which asks first.
safety.paths.protected.fix: Ask the repository owner if it must change. See the list with `lanekeeper-config explain project.protected_paths`.
safety.data.write.why: This command writes to protected data ({target}): `{cmd}`. Test data never goes into the owner's or production data.
safety.data.write.fix: Use the lane's own test database (assigned port, own container or test file). Lane ports are shown by `lanekeeper-port`. Protected targets are set in project.protected_data.
safety.data.unclear.why: This command touches protected data ({target}) and it cannot be told whether it writes: `{cmd}`.
safety.data.unclear.fix: A read-only query passes at once when the SELECT is written directly after -c or -e. For a write, switch to the lane's own test database.
safety.paths.config.why: `{path}` is a Lanekeeper settings file. Changing it can change the safety rules.
safety.paths.config.fix: Review the change before going ahead, then check it with `lanekeeper-config validate`.
safety.shell.unresolved.why: The command name is a variable or substitution (`{cmd}`), so it cannot be judged before it runs.
safety.shell.unresolved.fix: Write the command name literally, e.g. `git push ...`.
safety.config.broken.why: Lanekeeper settings have an error, so safety checks cannot run: {file} · {key}: {msg}
safety.config.broken.fix: Fix the settings file and check it with `lanekeeper-config validate`. Until then git changes, kills, deletes and browser runs are blocked.
safety.approve.model.why: `/lanekeeper:approve` works only when a person types it in the prompt.
safety.approve.model.fix: Ask the repository owner to type `/lanekeeper:approve <action>`.
safety.internal.why: The safety hook failed internally and blocked this call: {msg}
safety.internal.fix: Check the installation with `/lanekeeper:doctor`. If it keeps happening, report it with the error text.
approve.config_broken: No grant was created because the settings have an error: {file} · {key}. Check with `lanekeeper-config validate`.
approve.not_git: Grants can only be created inside a git repository.
approve.retry_bypass: The automatic resume now uses bypassPermissions: the resumed session runs any tool without asking, unattended. To go back, run `lanekeeper-retry mode default`.
approve.need_ref: Cannot tell which branch {action} is for. Name it: `/lanekeeper:approve {action} <branch>`.
approve.bad_ref: `{ref}` does not resolve to a commit.
approve.stamp_needed: A gate pass stamp for the same commit is also required: {stamp}
approve.granted: Owner grant recorded: {action} · {ref} · commit {head} · {ttl} min (expires {expires}) · one use. Only this commit can be applied.
chat.detailed: [lanekeeper] Reply guideline: in chat, give the contents, evidence and figures directly and in detail. Attach evidence as an artifact or file as well.
chat.summary: [lanekeeper] Reply guideline: keep chat replies short (result and decision first). Put evidence and detail in an artifact or file and link it.
handoff.start:
[Lanekeeper handoff] Session start ({src}). This project has a handoff file ({file}). It holds the current state only.
Do the following. 1) Read {file} from start to end. Its content is attached below; if it was cut, read the whole file ({path}). 2) Past history is in `{archive}/`. Do not read it whole; when you need something, find it with `grep -n '<keyword>' {archive}/*.md` and read only that part. 3) In your first reply, summarize the current state: in progress / next / waiting for answers / pitfalls. 4) Then start the work.

--- {file} ({shown}) ---
{excerpt}
--- end (whole file: {path}) ---
handoff.shown.summary: the head only; read the file for the rest
handoff.stop: [Lanekeeper handoff] Work newer than {file} was detected (a commit or a changed file). Update the handoff and then finish. {file} holds the current state only (target: {max} lines or fewer). 1) Append finished content (completed waves, answered questions, state that no longer holds) to the end of `{archive}/progress-<YYYY-MM>.md` as a `## <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> — <summary>` section. If it is hard to separate, run `lanekeeper-waves handoff archive "<summary>"` to append the whole current file. Never delete history. 2) Rewrite {file} whole: one line at the top with the archive location and how to search it (`grep -n '<keyword>' {archive}/*.md`), then the sections goals and owner decisions / branches and servers / in progress (table) / next / waiting for answers / system notes / resume commands. Keep items that still hold. 3) Commit both files together. After updating, tell the user that the session can be cleared (/clear). If this turn's change needs no handoff, state the reason in one line and finish.
handoff.oversize: [Lanekeeper handoff] {file} has {lines} lines, over the {max}-line target. Shorten it so a new session can read it to the end. If it is an accumulated file that keeps old sections, run `lanekeeper-waves handoff migrate` to move it whole to `{archive}/progress-until-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, then fill the new file with the current state. Otherwise move finished content to `{archive}/progress-<YYYY-MM>.md` and shorten what is left.
handoff.template:
# progress — current state ({date})

This file holds the current state only. Rewrite it whole every wave and append finished content to the end of `{archive}/progress-<YYYY-MM>.md`. Find past history with `grep -n '<keyword>' {archive}/*.md` and read only that part.{prev}

## Goals and owner decisions

## Branches and servers

## In progress

| Work | Branch / worktree | Status | Report |
|---|---|---|---|

## Next

## Waiting for answers

## System notes

## Resume commands
handoff.cli.over: {file}: {lines} lines, over the {max}-line target. If it is accumulated, move it with `lanekeeper-waves handoff migrate` and write the current state anew.
handoff.cli.rewrite: Now rewrite {file} whole as the current state and commit it together with the archive file.
handoff.cli.small: {file} has {lines} lines, within the {max}-line target, so it was not moved. Add --force to move it anyway.
handoff.cli.migrated: Moved {file} ({lines} lines) to {to} and wrote a fresh current-state file.
token.shrink: [Lanekeeper token guard] Usage reached {util}% ({src}). From now on split waves and turns into shorter units; keep a committable stable state at the end of each unit.
token.handoff: [Lanekeeper token guard] Usage reached {util}% ({src}). Keep waves and turns short and update the handoff file at the end of every wave.
token.handoff.guarded: [Lanekeeper token guard] Usage reached {util}% ({src}). Keep waves and turns short. The handoff guard asks for a handoff at the end of every wave; follow it immediately.
token.critical: [Lanekeeper token guard] Usage is {util}% ({src}): critical. Stop at a safe point now and finish the last handoff. Then notify the user and start no new work; ask whether to (a) wait for the automatic resume or (b) switch session, and wait. Check the exact value with /usage.
token.notify.title: Lanekeeper token guard
token.toggled.off: Token guard is off: stage detection and instructions are stopped.
token.calibrate.usage: Usage: lanekeeper-token calibrate [<weighted tokens>] | --five <0-100> [--seven <0-100>] [--at HH:MM] | --check. A number sets the fallback budget (no number = current usage of the window). --five/--seven add the percentages /usage shows as a calibration point (--at: when you read them; default now).
token.status.usage: Last {hours} hours (local transcripts, this machine only): output {output}, input {input}, cache read {cache_read}, cache write {cache_creation} ({msgs} replies). Weighted total {weighted} (= input + 1.25 cache write + 0.1 cache read + 5 output).
token.src.estimate: official usage plus an estimate of local use since it was read
token.src.local: local tokens of the last {hours} hours against the budget
token.calibrate.manual: Calibration point added: five-hour {five}, seven-day {seven} at {at} (account …{account}).
token.calibrate.noaccount: No account found in ~/.claude.json; a manual point needs the account.
token.calibrate.check.head: Calibration points of account …{account} (% per 1M weighted tokens between consecutive points of the same window):
token.calibrate.check.none: Fewer than two points in the same window; nothing to compare yet.
token.calibrate.check.note: Comparing these rates checks whether the cache read weight (0.1) fits; with fewer than two pairs per dimension this is only a list.
token.status.official: Official ({at}, {age} min ago, {fresh}, account …{account}): five-hour {five}% (resets {five_reset}), seven-day {seven}% (resets {seven_reset}).
token.status.mismatch: The official cache belongs to another account (…{cached}); the active account is …{account}. It is ignored until Claude Code refreshes it.
token.status.nocache: No official usage cache in ~/.claude.json (Claude Code writes it when it reads /usage).
token.status.fallback: Fallback: local tokens against {budget} weighted ({from}) → {util}%, stage {tier}.
token.status.uncalibrated: Budget not set (personal.token_guard.budget = 0) and no official cache: the guard is silent. Exact usage: /usage; then `lanekeeper-token calibrate --five <n>` adds it as a point.
retry.prompt: The previous work was interrupted by a usage limit. Continue the interrupted work to the end. If it is already complete, change nothing and only report the completed state.
retry.notify.title: Lanekeeper automatic resume
retry.notify.scheduled: Usage limit reached. Automatic resume scheduled for {at}.
retry.notify.off: Automatic resume is off, so the resume was skipped (/lanekeeper:auto-retry on to enable).
retry.notify.downgraded: bypassPermissions is not confirmed; resuming with the default permission mode (/lanekeeper:approve retry-bypass confirms it).
retry.notify.start: Limit reset: resuming the interrupted work.
retry.notify.failed: Resume failed (exit {code}). See the log in the Lanekeeper data folder (auto-retry/logs).
retry.notify.done: Work resumed. Continue in chat with: claude --resume {session}
retry.session.done: [Lanekeeper auto-retry] {count} finished automatic resume(s). Details: `lanekeeper-retry status`.
retry.status.off: Automatic resume: off (detection and resume are stopped)
retry.status.downgraded: (bypassPermissions is set but not confirmed, so default is used)
retry.toggled.off: Automatic resume is off: detection stops, and scheduled resumes are skipped.
retry.cancel.usage: Usage: lanekeeper-retry status | on | off | cancel <session id prefix|all> | mode <mode> | limits
retry.mode.warning: bypassPermissions lets the resumed session run any tool without asking, unattended. Use it only in folders you trust. An agent cannot turn it on. To accept this risk, type this in the Claude Code prompt yourself: /lanekeeper:approve retry-bypass
retry.mode.set: Permission mode of the resumed session: {mode}
terse.on: Terse mode is on for this repository.
terse.off: Terse mode is off for this repository.
terse.notGit: Not a git repository: the switch needs one. Set personal.terse in ~/.lanekeeper/personal.json instead.
dispatch.where: `lanekeeper-route explain <task>` shows the routing trace and `lanekeeper-check brief <file>` checks a brief. Run `/lanekeeper:doctor` to inspect settings.
dispatch.notify.title: Lanekeeper dispatch on hold
dispatch.config_error.why: A settings file has an error ({file} {key}: {msg}). Routing was judged with the defaults.
dispatch.config_error.fix: Run `/lanekeeper:doctor` to find and fix the error.
dispatch.brief_missing.why: No brief marker (`<!-- lanekeeper-brief v1 type=… lane=… -->`). A dispatch needs a brief.
dispatch.brief_missing.fix: Write a brief from `templates/briefs/` (impl, fix, mockup, research, review, docs, test) and paste it into the prompt or name the brief file.
dispatch.brief_incomplete.fix: Fill in the missing sections or statements and dispatch again. `lanekeeper-check brief <file>` checks it beforehand.
dispatch.brief_placeholder.why: The brief still has an unfilled placeholder `{{{name}}}`.
dispatch.brief_placeholder.fix: Replace every `{{…}}` placeholder of the template with a real value.
dispatch.type_unknown.why: The brief task type `{type}` is not in the routing table.
dispatch.type_unknown.fix: Set type= in the marker to one of: {known}.
dispatch.type_missing.why: The task type is unknown and no model was given.
dispatch.type_missing.fix: Add type= to the brief marker ({known}). `lanekeeper-route resolve <task>` tells you which model to use.
dispatch.model_missing.why: No model given. Routing for task `{task}` picks `{model}`.
dispatch.model_missing.fix: Pass model: "{model}" to the Agent call.
dispatch.model_unknown.why: Model `{model}` is not in the routing table.
dispatch.model_denied.why: Model `{model}` is on the denied list (routing.denied). Denied beats routing.
dispatch.model_denied.fix: Use the next model in the chain, `{next}`. To lift the ban, remove it from denied in `~/.lanekeeper/routing.json`.
dispatch.model_exhausted.fix: Use the next model in the chain, `{next}`.
dispatch.below_floor.why: Model `{model}` is below the floor `{floor}` of task `{task}`.
dispatch.below_floor.fix: Use `{next}`. Routing never goes below the floor.
dispatch.differ_violation.why: This task must use a model different from the implementer, and `{model}` is the implementer's model.
dispatch.off_chain.why: Model `{model}` is not in the chain of task `{task}` ({chain}).
dispatch.off_chain.fix: Use `{next}`, or fix type= in the brief marker if the task type is wrong.
dispatch.not_first.why: Model `{model}` is allowed, but routing's first choice is `{next}`.
dispatch.not_first.fix: Use `{next}` unless there is a specific reason.
dispatch.same_model.why: No model other than the implementer's is left, so `{model}` runs in a fresh context.
dispatch.same_model.fix: Have the lane report state that the review used the same model in a fresh context.
dispatch.wait.why: Task `{task}` never goes below `{floor}`. Waiting until the reset at {until}.
dispatch.wait.fix: Dispatch again after the reset. Use `/model` to switch the main session model.
dispatch.no_model.why: No usable model is left in the chain of task `{task}` ({chain}) after the denied list and the floor.
dispatch.no_model.fix: Check denied and the chain in `~/.lanekeeper/routing.json`. Use `/model` to switch the main session model.
dispatch.lanes_full.why: {count} lanes are live, the cap is {max}; the new lane `{lane}` cannot start.
dispatch.lanes_full.fix: Integrate and clean up finished lanes first. The cap is machine.lanes.max.
dispatch.load_hold.why: The 1-minute load is {load}, at or above the hold-new-lanes threshold {hold}. No new lane starts (messages to an existing lane are not held).
dispatch.load_hold.fix: Dispatch again when running lanes finish and the load drops below {hold}. `lanekeeper-slot check` shows the load and orphan processes. The threshold is machine.load.tiers.hold_new_lanes.
dispatch.load_light_only.why: The 1-minute load is {load}, at or above the light-only threshold {light}. Task type {task} runs heavy work (tests, builds, installs), so no new lane starts.
dispatch.load_light_only.fix: Light task types (routing weight: light) such as design, review, adversarial review, docs and mockups can still start. Dispatch this lane again when the load drops below {light}. The threshold is machine.load.tiers.light_only.
brief.not_found: The brief file {file} does not exist. Check the path.
route.head: Task {task} · chain {chain} · floor {floor}
route.note.same-model-fresh-context: no other model left; {model} in a fresh context (record it in the report)
route.result_wait: Result: do not dispatch — never below {floor}, waiting until {until}
route.result_none: Result: no usable model (check denied and the floor)
route.unknown_task: Task {task} is not in the routing table.
safety.slot.unwrapped.why: `{cmd}` competes with other lanes for the machine when run outside a slot ({kinds}).
safety.slot.load_stop_heavy.why: The 1-minute load is {load}, at or above the stop-heavy threshold {stop}. Heavy runs of verifier lanes ({lane}) stop first: `{cmd}`.
safety.slot.load_stop_heavy.fix: Run it again when the load drops below {stop}. Light review such as reading code can go on. Runs that already hold a slot are left alone. The threshold is machine.load.tiers.stop_heavy.
slot.guard.warn: `{cmd}` is a heavy run and should go through a slot ({kinds}). Run it again wrapped like this: `{wrap}`
slot.config_error: Stopped on a settings error: {key} in {file} — {msg}. Check it with `lanekeeper-config validate`.
slot.usage: Usage: lanekeeper-slot [--kind heavy|browser|heavy,browser] [--lane <id>] [--timeout <sec>] -- <command> | lanekeeper-slot status | lanekeeper-slot reap [--orphans [--dry-run|--kill]] | lanekeeper-slot check
slot.wait_load: Waiting: load is high (1-minute load {load}, threshold {max}).
slot.wait_busy: Waiting: all {count} {kind} slots are in use.
slot.timeout: No slot within {sec} seconds; the command was not run.
port.usage: Usage: lanekeeper-port get <name> [--lane <id>] | list | lease --lane <id> | release --lane <id> | check
port.no-lane: The lane is unknown. Add `--lane <id>` or run inside a lane worktree.
port.no-lease: Lane {lane} has no port lease. Lease one first with `lanekeeper-port lease --lane {lane}`.
port.unknown-name: No port named {name}. Use a protected port name or lane.<name> (machine.ports.lane_range.per_lane).
port.list_range: Lane range: base {base}, step {step}, names {names}, up to {max} lanes
port.problem.overlap: The lane step ({step}) is smaller than the ports per lane ({names}), so bands overlap.
port.problem.too-high: The last lane port ({last}) is above 65535.
port.problem.protected: Band {block} holds protected port {name} ({port}); that band is never assigned.
port.full: No free lane port band (max {max}). Clear finished leases with `lanekeeper-reap --apply` or widen machine.ports.lane_range.
wt.git_failed.fix: Check the message above, sort out the branch or path, then run again.
wt.no_commit.why: This repository has no commits yet, so a lane worktree cannot be created.
wt.no_commit.fix: Make a first commit, then run again (for example `git add -A && git commit -m "initial commit"`).
wt.integration_ambiguous.why: Several branches match the integration branch pattern: {branches}
wt.bad_id.why: `{id}` cannot be used as a lane name.
wt.bad_id.fix: Use up to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-` (for example l3).
wt.lanes_full.why: {count} live lanes reach the limit of {max} ({lanes}).
wt.lanes_full.fix: Remove finished lanes with `lanekeeper-worktree remove <id>` first. The limit is machine.lanes.max.
wt.path_exists.fix: Pass another `--path` or clear that folder.
wt.main_checkout.why: {path} is the main checkout and is never removed.
wt.main_checkout.fix: Name a lane worktree or its path.
wt.busy.why: Processes are running inside {path}, so it was not removed (PID {pids}).
wt.busy.fix: Check each PID above and stop it with `kill <PID>` (not pkill or killall, which match by name). Then run again.

wt.not_worktree.fix: Check the path with `git worktree list`. Lanekeeper never deletes a folder that is not a worktree.

wt.setup_skipped: No slot came free, so the setup command was skipped. Run `lanekeeper-worktree setup {id}` later.

Run `lanekeeper-reap --gate-lock` by itself in the main session to raise the dialog, or the owner types `/lanekeeper:approve clear-gate-lock` in the Claude Code prompt.

Where it is not blocked, `python3 -m pip install openpyxl` is enough.

rules.md.title: Rule catalog
rules.md.intro: The rules the plugin keeps, each with its reason, where it is enforced and what to do when blocked. A lane is a piece of work one subagent carries out on its own, with its own branch and its own folder (worktree). A wave is a set of lanes that run together and are merged at once. The controller is the main session that reviews lane results and merges them into the integration branch. The owner is the person who manages the repository, and the gate is the full verification command run before merging. This file is generated with `lanekeeper-rules render --write`; do not edit it by hand.
rules.manual.title: Rules
rules.manual.intro: Lanekeeper keeps the {count} rules below with hooks and commands. For each rule this page says what it blocks, why, and how to fix the work when it blocks you.
rules.manual.verdicts: A hook gives one of three verdicts. Block: the command does not run. Ask: the user is asked whether to go on. Note: the command runs and the hook says what to do next.
rules.manual.message: A block message has three lines: why it was blocked, how to fix it, and where to ask. To find the rule behind the code in a message (for example `safety.git.lane_commit`), run `lanekeeper-explain code <code>`. To see everything that is blocked right now, run `/lanekeeper:explain`.
rules.manual.order: The rules are grouped in the order a new user usually meets them: git and branches, file and command safety, processes and environment, models and briefs, sessions and handoff, quality and documents, and planned rules.
rules.manual.generated: This page is generated from `rules/catalog.json` with `lanekeeper-rules manual --write`. To change it, edit the catalog and generate it again.
rules.manual.group.git: Which branches lanes and the main session may commit to, merge into and push. The safety hook judges every `git` command before it runs.
rules.manual.group.safety: Blocks deletions that cannot be undone and commands that cannot be judged. Risky commands stay blocked even when the settings are broken.
rules.manual.group.process: Keeps lanes that share one machine away from each other's processes, ports and screen.
rules.manual.group.dispatch: Checks the model and the brief when a subagent is sent. The dispatch hook judges every Agent tool call before it runs.
rules.manual.group.session: Lets work continue after a session ends or a usage limit stops it.
rules.manual.group.quality: Keeps reviews, reports and documents to the same standard. Most of these are guided by commands and skills; a few are blocked by hooks.
rules.manual.group.planned: Rules in the catalog with nothing that enforces them yet.
xp.clear: Nothing is blocked or waiting right now.
xp.links.none: No linked documents. Link some under `explain.links` in the project settings.
xp.config_broken.what: The settings have {count} error(s). The first is {key} in {file}.
xp.config_broken.why: With broken settings the safety rules cannot tell what to block, so anything risky is blocked.
xp.config_broken.fix: Run `/lanekeeper:doctor`, fix the error, then confirm with `lanekeeper-config validate`.
xp.limit.what: The {model} model hit its usage limit. It frees up at {until}.
xp.limit.why: An agent cannot start on a model that is out of quota, and Lanekeeper will not go below the lowest model set for a task type.
xp.limit.fix: Run `lanekeeper-route explain <task>` to see the next usable model. If all are out, wait until {until}; with auto-retry on, work resumes then.
xp.limit_all.what: The account hit its usage limit. It frees up at {until}.
xp.limit_all.why: No model can start a new agent.
xp.limit_all.fix: Wait until {until}. With auto-retry on, work resumes then (`/lanekeeper:auto-retry status`).
xp.gate_lock.what: A verification gate is running, so merging is paused.
xp.gate_lock.why: If code changes while the gate runs, its result no longer belongs to a known commit.
xp.gate_lock.fix: Wait for the gate to finish. If it looks stuck, check `lanekeeper-reap`; clearing needs the owner to type `/lanekeeper:approve clear-gate-lock` in the prompt.
xp.lane_dead.what: Lane {lane} is marked running but has been idle for {min} min.
xp.lane_dead.why: The agent has probably stopped or hit a limit.
xp.lane_dead.fix: Run `/lanekeeper:resume` to plan the restart and start the lane again in its own worktree.
xp.lane_blocked.why: The lane marked itself unable to proceed, usually waiting for a decision or another lane.
xp.lane_blocked.fix: Read the lane's note (`lanekeeper-waves board`) and make the decision it needs.
xp.lane_failed.why: The agent ended with an error or review sent it back.
xp.lane_failed.fix: Check the last state with `/lanekeeper:resume`, put the reason in the brief and start it again.
xp.lane_review.why: The agent has finished and its result needs checking.
xp.progress_stale.what: {file} is older than the latest work.
xp.progress_stale.why: A new session continues from this file alone, so a stale one repeats finished work.
xp.progress_stale.fix: Move finished content to the archive, write the current state again, then commit.
xp.progress_missing.why: A session that picks up the work has nothing to read.
xp.progress_missing.fix: Create it with `/lanekeeper:init` or write the current state.
xp.progress_oversize.why: A new session reads only the beginning and misses the current state further down.
xp.progress_oversize.fix: Move the file to `{archive}/` with `lanekeeper-waves handoff migrate` and write only the current state anew.
xp.lane_dirty.what: Lane {lane} has {count} uncommitted change(s) in its worktree.
xp.lane_dirty.why: Uncommitted changes can be lost when a session ends.
xp.lane_dirty.fix: If the lane will use them, save them in a temporary commit. Discard only after the owner agrees.
xp.worktree_missing.what: The worktree {path} of lane {lane} is gone.
xp.worktree_missing.why: The ledger lists the lane but its folder is missing, so work cannot continue.
xp.worktree_missing.fix: Recreate it with `lanekeeper-worktree create {lane}`, or for a finished lane tidy the ledger with `lanekeeper-reap --apply`.
xp.worktree_unregistered.what: Worktree {path} (branch {branch}) is not in the lane ledger.
xp.worktree_unregistered.why: Nobody is known to own it, which makes cleanup hard.
xp.worktree_unregistered.fix: Leave it if in use; if finished, merge it and remove it with `lanekeeper-worktree remove`.
xp.lanes_full.what: {count} live lanes: the cap of {max} is reached.
xp.lanes_full.why: Too many lanes raise machine load and tests time out.
xp.lanes_full.fix: Land finished lanes and clean up their worktrees before opening another (`/lanekeeper:lanes`).
xp.slots_busy.what: All {kind} run slots are in use ({count} held).
xp.slots_busy.why: Running heavy jobs together slows the machine and causes false failures, so only the slot count may run.
xp.slots_busy.fix: See who holds them with `lanekeeper-slot status` and wait. `lanekeeper-reap` reclaims slots whose owner died.
xp.on_protected.what: You are on the protected branch `{branch}`.
xp.on_protected.why: Commits and merges there need the owner's grant.
xp.on_protected.fix: Work on a feature or lane branch. The owner grants landing with `/lanekeeper:approve`.

decide.need_options: At least two options are needed: --option "A=text".

review.prefail.ok: Failure before the fix is recorded

art.bad_slug: The slug "{slug}" cannot be used. Use letters, digits, Hangul, dot, underscore and hyphen only, with no path separator or "..".

defects.md.title: Defect register
defects.col.title: Title
defects.xlsx_missing: The workbook needs Python 3 with openpyxl (python3 -m pip install openpyxl). Only the Markdown file was written.
mockup.why: {file} changes the UI structure (elements or selectors) and no mockup decision is recorded
mockup.fix: Show a mockup (the current screen and the options) as an artifact first, create a decision with `lanekeeper-decide new <slug> --kind mockup --scope {file} …`, then record the owner's choice with `lanekeeper-decide answer` ({dir}). The decided marker <!-- lanekeeper-decision v1 status=decided kind=mockup scope={file} --> unlocks writes to this path; a pending decision does not
mockup.where: The "Mockup first" section of the README. To turn the check off set mockup.decision_required to false in .lanekeeper/config.json (a decision for the repository owner).
artifact.head: Before the report stage ends:
artifact.missing: The finished work was not published as an artifact. Publish it with the Artifact tool, with before and after captures and figures{fallback}.
artifact.fallback: (without the Artifact tool, build an HTML file with `lanekeeper-art report`)
artifact.xlsx: The newest verification workbook has problems ({items}). Check with `lanekeeper-check test-results` and rebuild with `/lanekeeper:test-report`.
safety.codegraph.no_index.why: `{path}` has no codegraph index. A call for this path already failed in this session, so another one fails the same way.
safety.codegraph.no_index.fix: It is in the index queue (`lanekeeper-index status`). Until the index exists, continue with grep and Read.
safety.codegraph.no_index_manual.why: `{path}` has no codegraph index. A call for this path already failed in this session, so another one fails the same way.
safety.codegraph.no_index_manual.fix: Continue with grep and Read. To build the index, queue it with `lanekeeper-index add {path}`.
cg.nudge: Callers of `{ident}` come back with their enclosing functions in one `codegraph_callers` call (projectPath: `{root}`). Use codegraph for flow and callers, grep for line numbers and strings. This note shows once per session.
search.rg_hint: Use `rg` instead of `grep -r` for text search. rg follows .gitignore, leaves node_modules and build output out and is faster. Sources with many Korean comments can be taken for binary files; search them with `rg -a`. To include ignored files too, use `rg -a --hidden --no-ignore -g '!node_modules' -g '!.git'`.
search.rg_missing: Text search uses `rg` (ripgrep) instead of `grep -r`. rg is not installed on this machine. Go on with grep for now. Tell the user once that `brew install ripgrep` (macOS) or the package manager installs it, and install it only when the user agrees. Search Korean sources with `rg -a`.
cg.dead_notice: `{path}` has no codegraph index{queued}. Do not call codegraph for this path again; continue with grep and Read.
cg.missing: codegraph is not installed. `/lanekeeper:init` installs it only after you agree (for example `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph`).
cg.not_git: `{path}` is not a git checkout, so it was not queued.
cg.worker_busy: Another index worker (pid {pid}) is working through the queue.
cg.usage: usage: lanekeeper-index add [path] | run | status | drop <path> | orphans [--apply] | metrics [--days N] [--json]
cg.orphans_none: No leftover indexes (indexes in folders that are no longer worktrees).
cg.orphans_fix: `lanekeeper-index orphans --apply` deletes only these indexes (the folders stay).
wt.index_queued: Added to the codegraph index queue (`lanekeeper-index status`).
doctor.codegraphOrphans.detail: {count} · {size} — list them with `lanekeeper-index orphans`, clean up with `--apply`
doctor.codegraphOldKey.detail: `index_on_worktree` is the old name — use `auto_index` instead
doctor.codegraphAutoExclude.detail: Lanekeeper added these to .git/info/exclude itself because `/lanekeeper:init` was not run: {lines}

xlsx.sum.note_ledger: {n} e2e ledger mismatches — see the "{sheet}" sheet.
xlsx.flaky.rerun_result: Failed in the main run -> rerun {result}

xlsx.ledger.not_in_run: {priority} ledger case · not in this run

load.orphan.dry_run: Listed only. To stop exactly these PIDs run `lanekeeper-slot reap --orphans --kill`.
load.orphan.kill_gone: PID {pid} has ended or is now another process; skipped.
load.notice.hold: The 1-minute load {load} is at or above the hold-new-lanes threshold {hold}. Do not start new lanes; check orphan processes with `lanekeeper-slot check`.
load.notice.light: The 1-minute load {load} is at or above the light-only threshold {light}. Start new lanes only for task types without heavy runs, such as design, review or docs (hold-new-lanes threshold {hold}).
load.notice.stop: The 1-minute load {load} is at or above the stop-heavy threshold {stop}. Heavy runs of verifier lanes are refused. Do not start new lanes; check orphan processes with `lanekeeper-slot check`.
q.no_suites: No quality suites are configured. List a command per kind under `quality.suites` in the project settings `.lanekeeper/config.json` (example: examples/quality-config.json in the plugin).
q.list.manual: (no command · the skill runs it and records it)
q.run.dirty: [quality] There are uncommitted changes. This result counts as stale, so the ship precheck will not use it.
q.run.load_refused: The slot refused the run because the load is high (exit 75). Run it again when the load drops.
q.run.manual: {kinds} have no command. Test as the skill describes, then record the result with `lanekeeper-quality record`.
q.xlsx_skipped: [quality] The workbook was not written (needs Python 3.8+ and openpyxl). The JSON result and the index are kept. See `lanekeeper-test-report env` for the install steps.
q.record.usage: usage: lanekeeper-quality record <kind> --verdict passed|failed [--from <json>] [--report <file>] [--total n --passed n --failed n --skipped n --fixme n]
q.index.done: [quality] index updated · {n} results ({legacy} in the older layout) · {dir}/index.json, INDEX.md
q.index.title: Test result index
q.index.intro: Test results by version, date and kind. `lanekeeper-quality index` rebuilds this file from the result files; do not edit it by hand.
q.pre.head: Ship precheck · HEAD {head}
q.pre.tree_dirty: There are uncommitted changes. Commit them and check again.
q.pre.ok: Passed: every required verification passed on the current commit.
q.pre.blocked: Blocked: {n} items did not pass. Ship verification cannot start.
q.pre.fix_failed: {kind}: read the failures, fix the cause, then run `lanekeeper-quality run {kind}` again. Do not weaken or skip tests.
q.pre.fix_weakened: {kind}: fewer tests than the previous passed result, more skipped or fixme tests, or a loosened threshold. Revert it, or, when the change is intended, the repository owner types `/lanekeeper:approve accept-quality {kind} --reason why` in the prompt.
q.pre.fix_manual: {kind}: this kind has no command. Test as the quality skill of category {category} describes and record it with `lanekeeper-quality record {kind}`.
q.pre.no_requires: No kinds are required before ship verification (`quality.ship.requires` is empty), so the precheck is off.
q.pre.advisory_head: Warning kinds (`quality.ship.advisory`, do not block shipping)
q.pre.advisory_warn: Warning: {items}. Not done before shipping, or a blocker finding is still open. Check and record it with its quality skill (for example `/lanekeeper:quality-ux-adversarial`), or move the kind to `quality.ship.requires` to make it block.
q.why.stale: changed since result commit {commit}: {files} and {more} more
q.why.not_ancestor: result commit {commit} is not in the current branch history
q.col.name: Test
q.report.title: Quality report {version}
q.report.lead_ok: The latest results of all {n} required verifications passed.
q.report.lead_bad: Some verifications did not pass, have no result, or are weaker than before. See the table and the known issues below.
q.report.no_issues: No test failed in the latest results.
q.report.no_excluded: No test was skipped or marked fixme.
q.report.history_line: {n} runs of {kinds} kinds in this version. The numbers of each run are in the run history sheet of the workbook.
q.accept.owner_only: An agent cannot accept a weaker result alone: this command needs the ticket from a confirmation dialog. Run `lanekeeper-quality accept <kind> --reason "why"` by itself in the main session to raise the dialog, or the repository owner types `/lanekeeper:approve accept-quality <kind> --reason why` in the Claude Code prompt.
dispatch.ship_precheck.why: The ship precheck did not pass ({items}). Ship verification starts only after the required verifications (unit, integration, gate, e2e and so on) passed on the current commit
dispatch.ship_precheck.fix: Run `/lanekeeper:ship-verify`. `lanekeeper-quality precheck --run` reruns every missing, stale or failed verification; fix failures and run them again. Do not weaken tests
dispatch.ship_precheck.advisory: Warning kinds did not pass ({items}). The UX adversarial check was not done before shipping, or its newest result has an open blocker finding. This does not block shipping; tell the owner (`/lanekeeper:quality-ux-adversarial`)
q.report.weakened: Verifications weaker than the previous passed result
docs.no_config: Docs sync is not configured. List the targets (name, paths) under `docs_sync.targets` in the project settings `.lanekeeper/config.json` (example: examples/docs-sync-config.json in the plugin).
docs.unknown_cmd: Unknown command {cmd}. Use map, apply, drafts, verify or check.
docs.bad_base: Cannot find the base {ref}. Pass a branch, tag or commit with --base.
docs.title: Docs sync — impact map
docs.summary: Base {ref} ({sha}) · {changed} changed files · {screens} changed screen files
docs.reason.vanished: phrase "{phrase}" left the screens but stays here
docs.reason.nearby: phrase "{phrase}" from the changed part of a screen appears here
docs.draft.gone: "{phrase}" — gone from the screens. Rewrite it for the new screen or remove it
docs.draft.nearby: check that the text around "{phrase}" still matches the screen
docs.draft.image: after recapturing {image}, match the text and callout numbers
docs.draft.new_phrases: New screen phrases (check whether they need explaining): {list}
docs.skipped: Phrases left out of the reverse index as too common: {list}
docs.apply_hint: `lanekeeper-docs apply` runs the commands above in order.
docs.verify_hint: `lanekeeper-docs verify` runs the checks above in order.
docs.gate.passed: Gate: passed — {total} required, {satisfied} met · {acked} acknowledged · {missing} unmet, {warnings} review warnings
docs.gate.failed: Gate: failed — {total} required, {satisfied} met · {acked} acknowledged · {missing} unmet, {warnings} review warnings. Fix the required documents in the same change (`lanekeeper-docs drafts` shows the drafts)
docs.note: base {ref} · {total} required · {missing} unmet · {acked} acknowledged · {warnings} review warnings
docs.suite_note: docs sync gate (project.docs_sync) — one test per target
legacy.item.project: project settings {old} (new name {new}; rename it with git mv)
safety.owner.accept.why: Accept the weakened {kind} test result? Commit {commit} · verdict {verdict} · passed {counts} · weakening: {weakened} · reason written by the agent: {reason}
safety.owner.accept.fix: Allow records this in accepted.json, and the ship check then lets this result through. Decline changes nothing.
safety.owner.gate.why: Remove the old gate lock? It has been there for {ageMin} min · process {pid} · command: {command}
safety.owner.gate.fix: Allow only if no gate is still running, because merges would stop waiting for it. Decline changes nothing.
safety.owner.subagent.why: A subagent asked for an owner decision, and a subagent's request cannot raise a dialog for the owner.
safety.owner.subagent.fix: Report the request to the main session. The main session runs the same command alone on one line, or the owner types `{slash}`.
safety.owner.headless.why: This session has nobody at the prompt to answer a dialog (`-p` or the SDK).
safety.owner.headless.fix: Ask the owner to type `{slash}` in an interactive session.
safety.owner.mode.why: Permission mode `{mode}` does not guarantee that a person sees the dialog.
safety.owner.mode.fix: Switch to `default`, `acceptEdits` or `auto`, or ask the owner to type `{slash}`.
safety.owner.variant.why: A dialog can only be raised for the plain command alone on one line, so that what is allowed is what runs. Chains, pipes, wrappers, paths, environment prefixes and added options do not qualify.
safety.owner.variant.fix: Run `lanekeeper-reap --gate-lock` or `lanekeeper-quality accept <kind> --reason "why"` by itself, with the reason as one quoted word of plain text, or ask the owner to type `{slash}`.
safety.owner.allow_rule.why: `{rule}` in {file} allows this command, so the dialog may never appear.
safety.owner.allow_rule.fix: Remove that rule, or ask the owner to type `{slash}`.
safety.owner.not_git.why: This folder is not a git repository, so there is nowhere to keep the ticket.
safety.owner.none.why: There is no {kind} result to accept.
safety.owner.none.fix: Record a result first with `lanekeeper-quality run {kind}`.
safety.owner.lock_none.why: There is no gate.lock to remove.
safety.owner.lock_active.why: gate.lock is only {ageMin} min old, so a gate may still be running.
safety.owner.lock_active.fix: Wait for the gate to finish. Only a lock older than `machine.slots.stale_after_min` can be removed.
owner.ticket.missing: This confirmation has no valid ticket. It was already used, or no dialog raised it. Run the command again to get a new dialog, or use `{slash}`.
owner.ticket.nonce: The ticket does not match the current dialog, so nothing changed. Run the command again to get a new dialog, or use `{slash}`.
owner.ticket.expired: The dialog was answered after its 10 minutes ran out, so nothing changed. Run the command again.
owner.ticket.content: What the dialog showed has changed since it was raised (a newer result, a new lock, or another reason), so nothing changed. Run the command again and read the new dialog.
doctor.ownerAllowRule.detail: `{rule}` in {file} covers `lanekeeper-reap --gate-lock` or `lanekeeper-quality accept`, so the hook refuses them instead of raising a dialog. Remove the rule or use `/lanekeeper:approve`
